findings.reason: as written the node either exceeds its granted write scope to instrument `lane_context.py`, or lands a counter whose entries cannot answer §25's question, wasting the working day of fleet picks the counter must run to produce any data at all.
findings.text: §24's write paths name `reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py` as the counter's only product file, but every read its Why enumerates executes one level down: `prompts.render` reaches all of them through the single call `lane_context.build(...)` at `reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py:323`, and the reads live in `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py` — the published lane document at `lane_context.py:597` (`local_lane_load`), the live run pointers at `lane_context.py:533` (`list_live`), and a foreign owner's profile cache and ledger stamp at `lane_context.py:574` (`_cached_run_time_profile`). A counter confined to `prompts.py` can therefore record at most one entry for the whole composition (plus the template load at `prompts.py:343`) — the same aggregate-then-mislabel shape §22 exists to fix — while §25's done-when demands the finer breakdown ("each read's median, 90th percentile and share of render time", and the read that dominates the picks whose render exceeds 2 s).
